#### Services Tab

This tab is not available for dead oil meters or flash gas meters.

The Services tab is used for configuring the Auto Estimate, Gas Day Projection, and Rescan services, as well as the Quality and Characteristics Download processes for each meter. Note that the Rescan service controls both SCADA Request and Late Data exceptions.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 600;height: 558;" />

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Auto Estimate">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Auto Estimate Sub-Tab</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Auto Estimate">

For FLOWCAL to auto estimate data, the service FcSrvAutoEstimate.exe must be installed and running.

The Auto Estimate service allows for the estimation of missing data until data can be provided from the field. If multiple gaps are present with data interspersed between, the estimated values used to fill each gap are determined independently.

Auto estimates are configured in the Meter Editor on a per-meter basis; they can also be configured for a list of meters using the Bulk Changes screen.

The data collection interval should be smaller than the auto estimating interval (Time Elapsed Before Missing) to minimize unneeded estimates, which would unnecessarily grow the database and affect performance. Auto estimate should only be running when the collection interval has skipped.

The Auto Estimate service is not applicable for gas line pack meters.

This feature is only available with the Service to Auto Estimate Missing Data Module.

- **Auto Estimate Enabled** - If set to "Yes", the Auto Estimate service is enabled for the meter.

- **Replace Estimated Data on Import** - If set to “Yes”, estimated data will be replaced by original data when it is imported.

  Auto estimated records are created as revision 1. Data imported into a period that has been auto estimated comes in both as a revision 0 record (beneath the auto estimated record) and as a revision 2 record, which will overwrite the auto estimate data. If source analysis or an auto edit is to be applied, it will be applied at this time, and a revision 3 record will be created in meter periodic values.

  If this option is set to “No”, the imported data is only brought in under the auto estimated record, and an exception is generated to indicate that imported data is being obscured by the estimated data.

- **Auto Estimate Record Only One Time** - If set to “Yes”, once data has been auto estimated, that data is no longer considered for estimation. This keeps the original estimate, regardless of any newer data that it might be based on.

  If set to “No”, changes to data used to generate the auto estimate can result in the records being re-estimated and adjusted as appropriate.

- **Log Missing Data in Exceptions Log** - If set to “Yes”, an exception is generated to flag records written by the Auto Estimate service as having missing data so that they can be evaluated, and data can then be imported if needed. To clear this exception, you must manually ignore it from the Exception Resolver.

  This missing data exception is in addition to the missing data exceptions that may occur on import.

- **Log Exception on Replacing Auto Estimate** - If set to “Yes”, an exception will be generated when an auto estimated record is replaced by imported data. To clear this exception, you must manually ignore it from the Exception Resolver.

- **Estimate Resolution** - The resolution that the Auto Estimate service will use when writing new records. This should match the resolution defined by the meter's characteristics. Options are 15 Minutes, Hourly and Daily.

- **Time Elapsed Before Missing** - Days or hours elapsed from the current datetime before data will be considered missing. Valid values are 0 to 30 (for days) and 0 to 23 (for hours).

- **Number of Prior Days Considered** - The number of days prior to the current date that the auto estimate service will scan to create an estimate for missing data or update a previous estimate. Valid values are 1 to 60.

  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Number Prior Days">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

  If you enter 60, the service will not examine data that is more than 60 days old.

  </div>

  Closed data within the specified time frame is not considered.

- **Adjust for Daylight Savings Time** - If set to "Yes", the Auto Estimate service will allow for a missing hour in the week after Daylight Saving Time begins. When the time reverts to standard time, one record will have double volume (for double flow time).

  If set to "No", the Auto Estimate service will estimate for the missing hour if a time change occurs.

- **Improve Estimate** - If set to "Yes", when more than one estimate technique is specified, the Auto Estimate service will re-estimate using a better technique as more information becomes available.

  FLOWCAL considers Estimate Technique 1 to be the best technique.

  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Improve Estimate">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

  <div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example-Improve Estimate">

  If Estimate Technique 1 is a point-to-point estimate, and there is no data after the missing data, then this technique cannot be performed, so the service would use Estimate Technique 2, if specified.

  If data is later provided that occurs after the missing data, but there is still missing data elsewhere, the Auto Estimate service will see that the data was originally estimated using Estimate Technique 2, but that new data is now available, so Estimate Technique 1 can now be used.

  </div>

  </div>

  If set to “No”, once data is estimated by Technique 2 or 3, it will not be re-estimated by a "better" technique, even if new data is provided.

- **Energy** - Determines how missing energy is calculated.

  - **Estimate from Data** - Energy will be estimated using the same technique as was used to estimate the volume.
  - **Calculate from Hv** - Energy is calculated by applying the heating value to the estimated volume. The heating value may come from a source assignment; if there is no source assignment, the heating value may be an estimated value.

  A source assignment may overwrite an energy value if the estimated data has been accepted.

- **Edit Reason** - When data is estimated, this edit reason will appear with the historical data. The Code field shows the associated code to help indicate the edit reason.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Techniques">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Auto Estimate Techniques</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Techniques">

A meter or location’s data must be rolled up, depending on the auto estimate technique selected.

- **Average Data** - All records preceding a period of missing data that fall within the specified number of prior days or hours will be averaged to derive the values that will be propagated forward.

  - **Skip No Flow** - If checked, records indicating that a meter experienced zero flow are not included when generating the average.
  - **Allow Use of Auto Estimated Data** - If checked previously auto estimated records that fall within the specified window will be included when calculating the average.

  Consider the data resolution when specifying averaging period.

- **User Data** - Missing data is populated with user-specified volume and energy or gross standard volume and mass. This is useful when a meter has gone out of service and needs to be populated with zeroes, or if a compressor has no meter on the fuel usage, but you have an estimate to use for balancing the system. Note that only volume and energy are populated; pulses, differential pressure, static pressure, temperature, and flow time will remain blank.

- **Curve Data** - Specify a starting volume, energy, base date, and decline factor. The specified volume and energy will be used on the base date and start declining by the factor specified. Over time the volume and energy estimate will diminish based on the decline factor. This technique may be used when a well test is done periodically, and the volume and energy is calculated for that point in time.

- **Point to Point Data** - When a gap is present, the record immediately preceding the gap and the record immediately following it will be evaluated, and the average of the difference between the two records will be determined for each data point. Starting from the first missing record, the previous value for a data point will be adjusted by the calculated value, creating a series of intermediate steps between the two field records. It will draw a straight line between the start and end points for differential pressure, pressure, temperature, volume, and energy.

  There must be data both prior to and after the missing data.

- **Reference Meter or Location Data** - A reference meter or location must be specified for this option. Any missing data is filled in using the values available at that time on the reference meter or location.

The **Multiplier** option allows you to specify a factor by which the reference meter or location's data is multiplied before being applied to the current meter or location.

- **Previous Day’s Data** - This technique populates each record with data provided for the meter exactly one day prior. This technique is useful if meters are cyclical.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Gas Day Projection">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Gas Day Projection Sub-Tab</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Gas Day Projection">

The Gas Day Projection service automatically projects flow values for a meter or location for the remainder of the gas day. These projected values are based upon historical data variables selected by the user and are calculated as an allocated percentage of a reference meter or location.

This feature requires the Gas Day Projection Volume Service module.

#### User Reference Data

Estimate based on the meter, reference meter, or location data.

- **Percentage Used** - The percentage of volume, energy, and mass used from the source record. This option projects any nonexistent daily data for the current day back one month. If any daily data exists that has actual hourly data and is complete or incomplete, the service does not project this record. If using a reference meter or reference location, the service only projects days where the reference has daily data.

  The percentage used only applies to the reference meter or location data.

#### User Historical Data

Estimate based on an average of previous days or hours as specified based on the meter or reference meter. This option projects current day only.

Current day is the day after the contract hour; otherwise, the current data refers to the previous day.

 

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="SCADA Request">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />SCADA Request Sub-Tab</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="SCADA Request">

This service scans the meter periodic values looking for missing data. Missing data queues a SCADA request to poll the meter device for the missing data. Requests can be seen from the SCADA Request Viewer.

The SCADA system must support this feature for it to work.

- **SCADA Request Enabled** - When set to "Yes", the SCADA Request service is enabled for the meter.

- **Log Rescan Data in Exceptions Log** - When set to “Yes”, an exception is generated when estimated data is written to the database. To clear this exception, you must manually ignore it from the Exception Resolver. This is a useful method for alerting office personnel to a meter not reporting in a timely fashion.

- **Rescan Frequency** - Determines if the service should rescan the meter periodic values hourly or daily.

- **Daily Rescan Hour** - Designates the hour of the day that the service should perform the scan.

- **Number of Retries Allowed** - The number of times that the service should request SCADA to attempt to collect data for missing hours. If no data is found after the specified number of rescans, the status in the FC_SCADA_REQUEST table is set to "N".

- **Time Elapsed Before Considered for Rescan** - Amount of time (days or hours) the service waits until it rescans for missing data. Valid values are 0 to 30 (for days) and 0 to 23 (for hours).

  Data is considered missing if it is older than the values entered.

- **Number of Prior Days Considered** - The time frame for which the service processes data. Specifies the number of days prior to the current date that the service will scan for missing data. Valid values are 1 to 60.

  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Number Prior Days 2">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

  If you enter 60, the service will not examine data that is more than 60 days old.

  </div>

  Closed data within the time frame specified is not considered.

  Make sure that you have installed and started the fcSrvAutoRecan.exe service.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Late Data">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Late Data Sub-Tab</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Late Data">

Using these settings, FLOWCAL will generate exception 4104 (Missing (late) data detected) when missing data is found and the wait period exceeds the amount of time specified in the Generate Late Data Exception After field. This service searches the prior number of days/hours specified, and generates an exception if there is missing data in at least one of those hours. The late data exception indicates that data should have arrived in FLOWCAL at a given time and is now late.

- **Late Data Exception Enabled** - When set to "Yes", late data exceptions are enabled for the meter.
- **Generate Late Data Exception After** - The length of time (in days or hours) to wait before generating the late data exception. This determines when to generate the late data exception, not the SCADA request exception.

Make sure that you have installed and started the fcSrvAutoRecan.exe service.

</div>

<span id="QualityDownload"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Quality Download">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Quality Download Sub-Tab</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Quality Download">

This tab allows for specified analysis data to be submitted as a SCADA request to a meter's remote terminal unit (RTU). Requests can be seen from the SCADA Request Viewer.

The SCADA system must support this feature for it to work.

- **Data to Download** - Once a Data to Download option has been selected and saved, a grid will display with the analysis data points. The following options are available:
  - **Current Analysis** - Most recent source analysis record from the assigned source (database table fc_gq_source_analysis).
  - **Last Hourly** - Current time minus 1 hour from the hourly rollups for the source assigned (database table fc_ffgq_hourly). Requires that the source is enabled for rollups and for hourly rollups.
  - **Last Daily** - Current day minus 1 day from the daily rollups for the source assigned (database table fc_ffgq_daily). Requires that the source is enabled for rollups.
  - **Last Monthly** - Current month minus 1 month from the monthly rollups for the source assigned (database table fc_ffgq_monthly). Requires that the source is enabled for rollups.
  - **Current Daily** - Current time from the daily rollups for the source assigned (database table fc_ffgq_daily). Requires that the source is enabled for rollups.
  - **None** - Do not download any analysis data (default).

<!-- -->

- **Send Current** - If checked, values will be provided by the current quality source, if one has been associated with the meter.
- **New Value** - Specify a new value for a parameter.
- **Send** - When clicked, the update request is written to the SCADA request table.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Characteristic Download">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Characteristic Download Sub-Tab</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Characteristic Download">

This tab allows for meter configuration and alarm parameters to be broadcast back to the remote terminal unit (RTU). In this way, an event that may have been missed can be corrected through FLOWCAL. Characteristic download requests can be seen from the SCADA Request Viewer.

This tab is only visible while in view mode.

The SCADA system must support this feature for it to work.

- **Send Current** - If checked, values will be provided by the current Master Meter Characteristic record, if one is provided for the meter.
- **New Value** - Specify a new value for a parameter.
- **Send** - When clicked, the update request is written to the SCADA request table.

</div>

</div>
